messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: Problems melting data that needs to be parsed
parts:
Here's one simple way:

library(stringr)
ddply(z, "x", function(df) data.frame(y = str_split(df$y, ";")[[1]]))

Hadley


On Thu, May 31, 2012 at 3:17 PM, Ed <ema...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I would like to melt data like the data frame z below into one that looks
> like data frame m.
>
>> x<-c(1,2,2,3)
>> y<-c("a;b;c", "b;c;d", "g;h", "f;g")
>> z<-data.frame(x,y)
>> z
>   x     y
> 1 1 a;b;c
> 2 2 b;c;d
> 3 2   g;h
> 4 3   f;g
>>
>>m
>    x y
> 1  1 a
> 2  1 b
> 3  1 c
> 4  2 b
> 5  2 c
> 6  2 d
> 7  2 g
> 8  2 h
> 9  3 f
> 10 3 g
>
> I have tried combinations of plyr, stringr, and base functions but haven't
> had any luck.  It seems like it should be easy.  I have used multiple search
> terms to find an answer, but cannot find a question that is the same.   I
> appreciate any help.
>
> Ed

parts:
Hadley,

Awesome.  This was very helpful.  I see now why I was not able to get it to work.

FYI...I did have to add one item to get all rows:
ddply(z, 'x', function(df) data.frame(y=str_split(str_c(df$y, sep=";", collapse=";"), ";")[[1]]))

Thank you,
Ed
